items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We were also joined by a young alto player from Wyoming, Ohio named Jimmie Smith.

ctx.x: One day Zack and Johnny came to my house and told me that there was a fellow in town from Michigan that wanted some musicians to play week-ends at a vacation camp not far from Kalamazoo, and they asked me if I would like to be a part of the group. I had never been more than a hundred miles from Cincinnati and this proposition sounded great to me. Zack and Johnny did not have to ask me twice if I wanted to go with them.

A few days later, we left Cincinnati with this fellow who was older than we were and he was the drummer. We were also joined by a young alto player from Wyoming, Ohio named Jimmie Smith. Jimmie was the second negro that looked like a white boy that I had come in contact with. I had gone south from Cincinnati but now I was going north. It was in the summer, maybe July or August, but the thing that excited me the most was that I was going further away from Cincinnati than I had ever been, leaving my father for the…

We arrived in Grand Rapids, Michigan and that was our headquarters. Every Saturday afternoon we would go to Kalamazoo by bus, and there we had a rendez-vous with someone who had a car and would meet us at the Y.M.C.A. to take us to this camp where we played Saturday nights, Sunday afternoon and evenings. We came back to Grand Rapids every Monday morning and spent the rest of the week days there. We all lived in the same rooming house except for the drummer, who's name I don't remember.
